name: Mediterranean Chicken w/ Marinade

ingredients.buy: 2 3/4 lb artichoke hearts, drained (about three 15 oz cans)
about 1 1/2 lb drained black olives (three 14.5 oz cans)

writer_notes: All 13 bought ingredient lines are used by a step; no step uses an unbought ingredient. Verified before submitting.

prose.intro_html:
This is the kind of dinner that looks like a restaurant plate and costs like a quiet Tuesday. Boneless chicken breasts get a lemon, garlic, and oregano marinade, then bake over a bed of spinach with artichoke hearts, grape tomatoes, and black olives, finished with a shower of crumbled feta. One casserole dish, one oven, and the whole week of dinners walks out lined up in the fridge.

Here is where the math does the talking. Every serving lands at 561 calories with 52 grams of protein and just 16 grams of carbs. That is a full plate that keeps you satisfied without the mid-afternoon crash, and it clears our 40-gram protein floor with plenty of room to spare. Big Mediterranean flavor, small carb footprint, and no special skills required.
prose.shop_smart:
The cart for this one is friendlier than it looks. Chicken breast is the anchor, so buy the family pack and let the freezer hold the rest for next time. You want 5 1/2 pounds of boneless skinless breasts, and evenly sized pieces bake more predictably than a mix of thin and thick.

Lean on the canned aisle here, because it is doing real work. The artichoke hearts come as three 15 ounce cans, drained, and the black olives as three 14.5 ounce cans, drained. Canned is the honest buy for both, since fresh artichokes are a project and a price. Grab a 14 ounce bag of fresh spinach, six lemons for juicing, and the feta at 1 pound 6 ounces, crumbled. Whole olive oil, a head of garlic, and your dried oregano, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes round it out, and those last four are pantry staples you likely already own.
prose.make_it:
Start with the marinade, because it needs the most patience. In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, the juice from your lemons, the minced garlic, the oregano, salt, and black pepper. Add the chicken to a large bowl or a sealable bag, pour the marinade over it, and toss or massage until every piece is coated. Seal it, refrigerate, and give it at least 4 hours, or overnight if you plan ahead. This is where the flavor gets in.

When it is time to cook, heat the oven to 400F. Spread the spinach across the bottom of a casserole dish sprayed with cooking spray or brushed with olive oil, and sprinkle the red pepper flakes over the top. Lay the marinated chicken breasts on the spinach, then scatter the artichoke hearts, grape tomatoes, and black olives over and around the chicken. Pour any marinade left in the bag right on top.

Bake covered for 25 minutes, giving thicker breasts a few extra if they need it. Pull it out, top each piece with the crumbled feta, and slide it back in uncovered for 5 more minutes to warm the cheese. Let the whole dish rest 5 minutes before you slice, so the juices settle instead of running out.
prose.portion_html:
This recipe is built to make 14 servings, and the fair way to split it is to weigh, not eyeball. Set your empty container on the scale and zero it out, then weigh the full baked dish and divide that number by 14. That is your target weight per container. Portion each one to hit it, spooning a little of the chicken, the spinach, and the artichoke, tomato, olive, and feta medley into every box so no container gets shorted on the good stuff.

Weighing beats guessing every time. Guess and your first few boxes are heavy, your last few are sad, and the macros stop being true. Weigh and all 14 land at 561 calories with 52 grams of protein, exactly as promised.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is the part that matters when the plan has to survive a real budget. This whole thing comes out to ${{cost_ps}} per serving. That is a lemon-marinated, feta-topped Mediterranean dinner with 52 grams of protein, for less than what a single fast-food combo costs you, times 14 nights you do not have to think about dinner.

Cheap does not have to mean sad, and expensive does not have to mean good. This plate proves both.

head.description: Baked Mediterranean chicken with a lemon-oregano marinade, spinach, artichoke hearts, tomatoes, olives, and feta. 561 calories and 52g protein per serving, 14 meal-prep dinners.
head.keywords: mediterranean chicken, baked chicken meal prep, high protein dinner, feta chicken, lemon oregano chicken, artichoke chicken, low carb meal prep, budget meal prep
steps: In a small bowl, whisk together the marinade: olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Add the chicken breasts to a large bowl or sealable bag with the marinade. Toss or massage to coat, seal, and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Spread the spinach across a casserole dish sprayed with cooking spray or olive oil, and sprinkle the red pepper flakes over the top.
Lay the marinated chicken on the spinach, then scatter the artichoke hearts, grape tomatoes, and black olives over and around the chicken, pouring any leftover marinade on top.
Bake covered for 25 minutes, adding a few minutes for thicker breasts.
Top each piece with crumbled feta, return uncovered for 5 minutes, then rest 5 minutes before slicing and portioning.
